flawed_step: No numbered proof was supplied. The first necessary nontrivial step—combining the Hamiltonian cycles in individual vertex-neighbourhoods into one cycle spanning the whole graph—is unjustified. The explicit locally Hamiltonian graph below has no Hamiltonian cycle.
counterexample: Let V={a,b,c,x,y,p1,p2,p3,q1,q2,q3}. Its complete edge set is {ab,bc,ca,xa,xb,xc,ya,yb,yc, p1a,p1b,p1x, p2b,p2c,p2x, p3c,p3a,p3x, q1a,q1b,q1y, q2b,q2c,q2y, q3c,q3a,q3y}. This is obtained from the triangular bipyramid on {a,b,c,x,y} by inserting one vertex into each of its six triangular faces, so it is a maximal planar graph. Directly, its induced neighbourhoods have the following Hamiltonian cycles: N(a): b-p1-x-p3-c-q3-y-q1-b; N(b): a-p1-x-p2-c-q2-y-q1-a; N(c): b-p2-x-p3-a-q3-y-q2-b; N(x): a-p1-b-p2-c-p3-a; N(y): a-q1-b-q2-c-q3-a. For each pi or qi, its three neighbours form one of the original facial triangles, hence form a 3-cycle. Thus the graph is locally Hamiltonian. Nevertheless, deleting S={a,b,c,x,y} leaves six isolated vertices p1,p2,p3,q1,q2,q3. A Hamiltonian graph must satisfy components(G-S)<=|S|, since deleting |S| vertices from a spanning cycle leaves at most |S| path segments. Here components(G-S)=6>5=|S|, so no Hamiltonian cycle exists.
assessment_summary: The proposed local-to-global implication fails. The explicit 11-vertex maximal planar graph is locally Hamiltonian, as verified by concrete neighbourhood cycles, but a five-vertex deletion produces six components and therefore certifies non-Hamiltonicity.
